findingMessages.doc-cli-orphaned-library-error-doc: The doc comment 'Why `--library DIR` can't be opened; for a library open in another program, how to work with that one instead (issue #99)' is attached to library_warnings, which only prints warnings; it describes library_error two items below. rustdoc and IDE hover show the wrong contract for both functions.
findingMessages.doc-cli-mcp-connect-comment-describes-ru: The --connect comment in mcp() says a non-address token such as a command id 'leaves the address at its default so the command is still consumed next', but mcp has no command tokens: such a token becomes a FILE and immediately fails with 'FILES, --demo and --library apply to headless mode only'. The comment was copied from run(), whose filter also differs (run rejects tokens containing '='), so the two parsers are documented as identical while behaving differently.
findingMessages.doc-cli-run-output-ms-on-failure: USAGE promises one JSON line per command shaped {"command", "ok", "result" | "error", "ms"}, but a failed step is emitted as {command, ok:false, error} with no ms field. A script parsing the documented shape (e.g. summing ms) breaks on the first failure line.
findingMessages.doc-cli-render-extension-hint-stale: render's unknown-extension error tells users to 'use .jpg .png .tif .webp .avif .dng', omitting .jxl and .psd, which USAGE advertises for render and ExportFormat::parse (crates/engine/src/export.rs:36-50) accepts. Users following the error text are steered away from supported formats.
findingMessages.doc-cli-module-header-omits-subcommands: The crate-level usage block lists subcommands but omits `look extract` and `ai compare`, both dispatched in main() and documented in USAGE, and omits denoise-serve's --max-connections. Readers of the source/rustdoc get an incomplete command inventory.
findingMessages.doc-desktop-gpu-crash-notice-wrong-on-ma: After a GPU startup crash the user-facing notice says to re-enable 'Settings > Performance > Use the GPU for rendering' and to try LIGHTCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND=dx12, vulkan or off. The Settings checkbox is actually labelled 'Use GPU rendering when available', and on macOS (a supported host for this binary) neither dx12 nor vulkan is a usable backend; metal, which parse_backends accepts (crates/gpu/src/backend.rs:11), is not mentioned. A macOS user following the recovery instructions sets a backend that cannot initialise.
